key_insight: Facts seen only once during training—called monofacts—are identified as a key factor governing LLM scientific discovery capacity.
engineering_relevance: For materials-discovery models, training-data design should consider monofact rates alongside dataset size and diversity.
method: Model discovery capacity through a missing-probability-mass framework.
Directly vary monofact rates in materials-science and regulatory-genomics training sets.
Test discovery outcomes across model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets.
evidence_signal: Higher monofact rates consistently yielded more discoveries across two open-weight model families, with additional experiments indicating the effect was not explained by training-set diversity alone.
watch_item: Cross-domain transfer was observed when paired with in-domain data; the abstract does not establish generalization to arbitrary scientific domains.
paper_title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
